subject: Q3 kickoff: owners' OKR clarifications, QBR ask-list and stakeholder asks
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Reynolds <kara@acme.com>
Date: Wed, May 19, 2027 at 09:12 AM -07:00
Subject: Q3 kickoff: owners' OKR clarifications, QBR ask-list and stakeholder asks

Team —

We need to lock down owner-level OKRs and the QBR ask-list by next Friday so we can circulate the packet to execs and ACME ahead of their review. I attached the Q3_OKR_template.xlsx and a draft QBR_agenda_v2.pdf. Please do the following before EOD Monday:

- Owners: fill the template rows for your top 3 objectives, the lead metric, and the 2 main risks. (owner = person responsible for delivery)
- PMs: add one example customer impact story or KPI to demonstrate value for each objective.
- Ops/Eng: flag any capacity or infra blockers that would prevent a canary launch in week 6.

Notes/constraints: we should avoid adding new cross-org dependencies unless they come with a committed owner. ACME requested 2 slides with customer impact and an ask list (budget/time) — included below.

Karthik / Marissa / Logan — can each of you confirm owner names in the template and add a single line on risks? Kara, feel free to reply with any ACME priorities so we can fold them into the QBR ask-list.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q3_OKR_template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB), QBR_agenda_v2.pdf (pdf, 320KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Reynolds <kara@acme.com>
Date: Wed, May 19, 2027 at 11:07 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 kickoff: owners' OKR clarifications, QBR ask-list and stakeholder asks

Kimberly —

Thanks for the note. Quick updates from my side (I'll edit the spreadsheet too):

1) Objective 1 (Inference latency / p50): Owner = Logan Wright; lead metric = p50 latency at 95th percentile traffic; risk = burst traffic causing degraded batching (mitigation: increase pre-warmed slots + KV cache tuning).
2) Objective 2 (Unit cost reduction): Owner = myself; lead metric = $/1000 tokens served; risk = model regression when we quantize aggressively (mitigation: add eval gate in Redwood Optimize).
3) Objective 3 (Enterprise adoption): Owner = Marissa Cole; lead metric = #Dedicated contracts signed (Q3 target 6); risk = procurement delays at large customers (ask: legal resource for templated SOW).

Operational blockers: planned infra maintenance in week 5 may temporarily limit Dedicated burst capacity — Ops needs to confirm safe windows.

I'll add these to the template and flag the risk column. Also suggest we add a one-line 'rollback' play for Objective 2 (fallback to float16 model in case of quality regression).

On the QBR asks: ACME will likely want clearer cost impact per-seat for Dedicated; Kara, can you confirm the procurement timeline?

-Karthik

Adding my notes — I'll own Objective 3 as discussed. Quick asks from GTM side:

- Please include a conversion funnel metric for the enterprise pipeline (SQL->POC->Closed) so ACME sees the funnel health.
- For the QBR packet: two slides for ACME — one on platform roadmap and one on customer outcomes. I'll draft the outcomes slide; Kimberly, can you own the roadmap bullets?

Also, I updated the spreadsheet: changed the 'owner' field for Objective 1 to Logan, and added a note under risks for Objective 2 about E2E latency regressions during A/B.

Attachments: ACME_SOW_template.docx (referenced; not attached in this mail thread)

-Marissa

Date: Thu, May 20, 2027 at 08:15 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 kickoff: owners' OKR clarifications, QBR ask-list and stakeholder asks

Hi Kimberly and team —

Thanks for looping us in. ACME priorities for the QBR:

- Clear cost per 1k tokens and an estimate for Dedicated seat pricing if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool (we need topline numbers by next Thursday).
- A short readout on reliability / SLA improvements in the last 6 months (one slide).
- A list of 'askable' product features with rough ETA (ideally categorized must-have / nice-to-have).

Procurement timeline: Procurement will start internal review on June 1, but legal review typically takes 3 weeks. If you can give an initial SOW by May 27 we can speed a parallel review.

Best,
Kara Reynolds
Senior Procurement Manager — ACME Corp

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, May 21, 2027 at 15:30 PM -07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 kickoff: owners' OKR clarifications, QBR ask-list and stakeholder asks — final decisions

Team — thanks for the quick turn. Summary and decisions (finalized in the template):

- Objective 1 (Latency): Owner = Logan Wright. Lead metric captured in template; risk mitigation = pre-warm + KV-cache tuning.
- Objective 2 (Unit cost): Owner = Karthik Iyer. Added rollback plan (float16 fallback) and an eval gate in Redwood Optimize.
- Objective 3 (Enterprise adoption): Owner = Marissa Cole. Added funnel metric (SQL->POC->Closed).

Action items (owners):
- Logan: complete latency deck slide + one-line technical mitigation by Mon 5/24.
- Karthik: add eval plan and rollback steps in the template by Mon 5/24.
- Marissa: draft ACME outcomes slide and SOW first-pass by Thu 5/27.
- Kimberly: assemble QBR packet, finalize 6 slides for execs, and share with Kara by Fri 5/28.

I've uploaded the updated template and agenda to the shared drive: https://docs.redwood.com/drive/Q3-OKR-template (see 'final' version). Kara: appreciate the procurement timeline — we'll prioritize the SOW draft for 5/27.

If there are no objections I'll mark this thread as sign-off and move to create the QBR packet.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
